1.note: David is speaking of Yahweh as if he were a **shepherd** who cares for and protects his sheep. If this image communicates well in your language, please use it. If not, you could express this as a comparison as in the UST.

David is emphasizing a positive meaning by using a negative word, **nothing**, together with a mild expression, **I will lack**, that is the opposite of the intended meaning. If it would be helpful in your language, you could emphasize the positive meaning in a strong way. Alternate translation: [I will have everything I need] or [I will be completely satisfied]

2.q: בִּ⁠נְא֣וֹת דֶּ֭שֶׁא יַרְבִּיצֵ֑⁠נִי עַל־מֵ֖י מְנֻח֣וֹת יְנַהֲלֵֽ⁠נִי
2.note: David continues to draw an extended comparison between Yahweh’s care for him and a shepherd caring for his sheep. Here David compares Yahweh’s care for him to a shepherd who brings his sheep to **green pastures** and **waters of rest**. If it would be helpful for your readers, you could express this as a comparison. Alternate translation: [He gives me what I need to be satisfied and at peace, like a shepherd who provides pasture and water for his sheep]

By **He makes me lie down**, David means “He takes me to where I can lie down” or “He lets me lie down.” You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [He takes me to green pastures where I can lie down] or [He lets me lie down in green pastures]
Here the word **to** could mean: (1) “to” as in the ULT or (2) “alongside.” Alternate translation: [alongside]

The phrase **waters of rest** could refer to: (1) still or calm bodies of water. Alternate translation: [calm waters] or [quiet waters] or (2) the location of the water and refer to bodies of water that were located at resting places. Alternate translation: [waters at resting places]

3.q: נַפְשִׁ֥⁠י יְשׁוֹבֵ֑ב יַֽנְחֵ֥⁠נִי בְ⁠מַעְגְּלֵי־צֶ֝֗דֶק לְמַ֣עַן שְׁמֽ⁠וֹ
3.note: Here David is speaking of Yahweh as if he were a shepherd who **restores** his **soul** and **leads** him **in right paths**. David means that Yahweh renews his spiritual and emotional strength and guides him to live in a way that pleases Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a comparable expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [He renews my spiritual strength. He guides me to live righteously for the sake of his name] or [He renews my spiritual strength. He guides me regarding how to live in the right way, for the sake of name]

Here David is using the term **my soul** to mean himself from the perspective of his spiritual or emotional existence. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [me] or [my spiritual strength]
Here David is using the term **name** to represent who God is or to refer to God’s reputation. Alternate translation: [for the sake of his reputation] or [to bring honor to himself]

4.q: גַּ֤ם כִּֽי־אֵלֵ֨ךְ בְּ⁠גֵ֪יא צַלְמָ֡וֶת לֹא־אִ֘ירָ֤א רָ֗ע כִּי־אַתָּ֥ה עִמָּדִ֑⁠י שִׁבְטְ⁠ךָ֥ וּ֝⁠מִשְׁעַנְתֶּ֗⁠ךָ הֵ֣מָּה יְנַֽחֲמֻֽ⁠נִי
4.note: David continues to draw an extended comparison between his relationship with God and a shepherd caring for his sheep. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the comparison. Alternate translation: [Even though I experience great danger or hardship, I will not be afraid because you protect and guide me like a shepherd protects and guides his sheep with his rod and staff]

The phrase the ULT translates as **the valley of deep darkness** could be translated: (1) as the ULT does and refer to a dark valley or ravine. Alternate translation: [through a dark valley] or (2) as [the valley of the shadow of death.] Alternate translation: [through the valley of the shadow of death]

David is using the adjective **evil** as a noun to mean things that people might do to harm him. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [I will fear no harm] or [I will fear no danger]

If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [because you are with me, I will fear no evil]

Here, **rod** and **staff** represent the shepherd’s protection and guidance. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [your protection and guidance comfort me]

5.q: תַּעֲרֹ֬ךְ לְ⁠פָנַ֨⁠י ׀ שֻׁלְחָ֗ן נֶ֥גֶד צֹרְרָ֑⁠י דִּשַּׁ֖נְתָּ בַ⁠שֶּׁ֥מֶן רֹ֝אשִׁ֗⁠י כּוֹסִ֥⁠י רְוָיָֽה
5.note: David is speaking of God’s care and provision as if God were a host preparing a feast for an honored guest. The image includes arranging a table with food, anointing the guest’s head with oil as a sign of welcome and honor, and filling the guest’s cup to overflowing. If this image communicates well in your language, please use it. If not, you could express this as a comparison. Alternate translation: [In front of my enemies you provide for me and honor me like a host preparing a feast for a special guest]

Here, **before my face** represents being in David’s presence. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in my presence] or [for me]

The implication is that God provides for and protects David even when he is surrounded by those who wish to harm him. This demonstrates God’s protection and care in dangerous situations. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [while my enemies watch] or [even though my enemies are present]

In that culture, putting scented **oil** on a guest’s head was a symbolic action by which a host showed honor to and welcomed a guest. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [you have honored me by anointing my head with oil] or [you have honored and welcomed me by anointing my head with oil]

In that culture, filling a guest’s wine cup to overflowing was a symbolic action by which a host showed that they intended to abundantly and liberally provide for their guest. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [you have blessed me abundantly]

6.note: If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **goodness** and **covenant faithfulness**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [Yahweh will continually show me how good he is and how faithful he is to his covenant]

The Hebrew word that the ULT translates as **and I will dwell** could be: (1) a contracted form of the Hebrew word that means “dwell,” in which case it should be translated as the ULT does, or (2) a form of the Hebrew word meaning “return.” Alternate translation: [and I will return and go]

David is using the phrase **the house of Yahweh** to refer to Yahweh’s tabernacle (tent of meeting), where Yahweh was worshiped, as if it were a **house** in which Yahweh lived. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I will dwell in the tabernacle of Yahweh] or [and I will dwell in Yahweh’s sanctuary]

The implication is that David will dwell with God for his entire life. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [for my whole life] or [as long as I live]
